title: Quantitative C^{1,α} estimate for Δw = div F when F is a small Campanato perturbation of Dw (Caccioppoli, Morrey and Campanato iterations; Giaquinta–Martinazzi Ch. 5, §5.4)
statement: Let m ≥ 1, k ∈ ℕ and 0 < α < 1. There is ε₁ > 0 such that for all K ≥ 0 and R > 0 there is C ≥ 0 with the following property. Let x₀ ∈ ℝ^m, w : ℝ^m → ℝ^k C¹ on B_R(x₀), F : ℝ^m → L(ℝ^m, ℝ^k) continuous on B_R(x₀), with ‖w‖ ≤ K and ‖F‖ ≤ ε₁‖Dw‖ + K on B_R(x₀) (operator norms); assume (H_F): for every ball with closedBall(x, ρ) ⊆ B_R(x₀), ρ > 0, there is a constant c ∈ L(ℝ^m, ℝ^k) with ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ‖F − c‖² ≤ ε₁∫_{B_ρ(x)} ‖Dw − ⨍_{B_ρ(x)} Dw‖² + Kρ^{2α}∫_{B_ρ(x)} ‖Dw‖² + Kρ^{m+2α}; and assume Δw = div F weakly in B_R(x₀) (∫ Σ_j ⟨Dw e_j, Dζ e_j⟩ = ∫ Σ_j ⟨F e_j, Dζ e_j⟩ over B_R(x₀) for all C¹ ζ with compact support, tsupport ζ ⊆ B_R(x₀)). Then ‖Dw(x)‖ ≤ C and ‖Dw(x) − Dw(y)‖ ≤ C‖x − y‖^α for all x, y ∈ B_{R/4}(x₀).
